_comment: Open questions that are not rulings. Items in group 'copy' need Brian's printed copy and stay as read until he answers; the autopilot decides the rest (AUTOPILOT.md, Mission 4). tools/decisions_page.py merges these with every proposed rulings/R-nnn.md into build/decisions.html. Remove an item once its answer has landed.

items.title: Map E: which Delta channels are major rivers?
items.context: The Delta branches and canals are printed at a middle width. We disagree with the second database on 72 hexsides (38 major→minor, 34 minor→major). Another 62 rows are the Fayum lake shore, the Nile running through a hex, or a channel the second database puts on the next hexside. All are left as read.
options: My Terrain Key says which channels are major (see note)
Take the second database's classes for the 72 disputed hexsides
Leave them as read

items.title: Hill bands: ridge or slope?
items.context: Map E recorded 42 hill bands on rough ground as ridge, because the band lies on both sides of the hexside (the extractor's ridge rule). Measured the same way, 9 of Map D's 16 open hill-band rows are ridges (D2408|D2508, D2531|D2631, D2532|D2631, D2631|D2632, D2729|D2829, D2811|D2812, D2827|D2928, D2828|D2829, D2812|D2912; D3115|D3214 borderline).
options: Two-sided bands are ridges: set Map D's 9 to match Map E
Bands are slopes: revert Map E's 42 to slope
My Terrain Key says something else (see note)

items.title: Blue railways: finished or unfinished in 1940?
items.context: #64 made the blue Matruh–Capuzzo–Tobruk line on Map C an unfinished railroad. The Benghazi–Barce line (Map A) and the coast line east of Matruh (Map D: Fuka, Baggush) are also blue on the scan but kept as railroad.
options: Blue means unfinished everywhere: make A and D match C
Blue is just print colour: all three are railroad
Per line (see note)

items.title: Which side is higher at C0323|C0423?
items.context: Our band-side convention says C0323 is higher; the second database says C0423, a rough hill ringed by hachures. If the database is right, the convention needs a second look at depressions.
options: C0323 is higher (our convention)
C0423 is higher: revisit the convention
Can't tell from my copy either

items.title: Rows the scan cannot settle
items.context: A 33, B 112, C 22, D 50, E 207 rows are left as the extractor read them. Every key is in its sheet's EXTRACTION.md entry; only a physical copy can settle them.
options: Leave them as read
I'll check my copy for a sheet (see note)

items.title: SPI 20.67: where is the Axis replacement-type chart?
items.context: It is not printed on either player chart set or the shared sheet in the archive.org scan (every chart heading on jp2 111–178 checked).
options: My copy has it (see note for where)
Not in my copy either: record it as a known gap

items.title: Formation charts 19.31–19.33: two low-confidence reads
items.context: The symbol grids were read with less confidence in two spots (noted in data/tables/formation-organisation.json): the 5th Light's second infantry battalion, and which Ramcke battalion is the heavy-weapons one.
options: Both reads are right
One or both are wrong (see note)

items.title: German unit characteristics, ID codes c and d: CPA 30† or 30**?
items.context: The German chart set (and the community scan) print the CPA of ID codes c and d as 30 with a dagger, which the 4.46c key never defines; the copy of the chart on the Commonwealth side prints 30 with a double asterisk (keeps its CPA whatever is assigned). Recorded as 30†. Same chart: ID code v prints a lone asterisk in the close-assault column, recorded as offence '*', defence blank.
options: My copy prints 30** (or explains the dagger)
Leave as read

items.title: Group One: which counter is the el Grein garrison?
items.context: 60.31 places an 'el Grein Garrison' at C1715. The Italian Minor Garrison sheet has no counter by that name; the only one not named for another place is EGUG, and the scenario data uses it. Unconfirmed.
options: EGUG is el Grein
Another counter (say which)
Leave as read

items.title: German Tank and Gun chart (4.49): three misaligned rows
items.context: Both scans print Pz III E as 25, 1, -, 4, 3, 4/4, 3, 4/4, 3 across CPA to BAR, and 7.62cm Pak(R) and Marder III one cell short. Read as: Pz III E vulnerability -, armour 3, Off/Def 4/4, fuel 3, BAR 0; Pak(R) CPA 15 (like every towed gun), anti-armour 9, vul 2, Off/Def 1/1, fuel 1; Marder III CPA unknown, anti-armour 9, vul 2, armour 2, Off/Def 3/2, fuel 2, BAR 0. 5cm Pak 38 Off/Def printed 1½1, read 1/1.
options: My copy agrees with the realignment
My copy differs (say how), or gives the Marder's CPA
Leave as read

items.title: Axis coastal ship counters: three of 1,000 tons and one of 2,000?
items.context: 56.31 puts each coastal ship's tonnage on its counter. We have no scan of the counter sheet; the VASSAL module (errata applied) has four: A, B and C at 1,000 tons, D at 2,000. Recorded so in data/tables/axis-coastal-ships.json.
options: My counters agree
My counters differ (say how)
Leave as read

items.title: Air Reconnaissance of Axis Naval Convoys Table (42.53): where is it?
items.context: 42.53 resolves the Commonwealth's convoy reconnaissance on this table, but it is not on the archive.org chart pages (jp2 95-191), and the Common Charts index does not list it. Without it convoy reconnaissance has no resolution. The Axis Airplane Reinforcement Schedule (34.87) is missing the same way.
options: My copy has it (page and values in a note)
My copy lacks it too: decide a procedure as a ruling
